headline: 9 units of Fire Service fire breaks out at sweater factory in Gazipur
summary: Over 100 workers were safely evacuated from the 8-story Metrics sweater factory in the Degerchala Fakir Market area.
details: A fire broke out at the Metrics sweater factory in the Degerchala Fakir Market area of Gazipur city on Saturday afternoon.
The blaze started around 3:00 PM on the third floor of the eight-story building and quickly spread to surrounding areas.
Nine units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, including units from Gazipur Chowrasta Modern, Konabari, Gazipur, and Rajendrapur stations, were deployed to control the blaze.
Firefighters reported that over 100 workers were safely evacuated from the building during the operation.
As of 4:45 PM, the fire had not yet been brought under control. The cause of the fire and the extent of the property damage have not been immediately known.
Gazipur Chowrasta Modern Fire Station officer Mo. Hiron Mia confirmed that efforts to control the fire are ongoing and no casualties have been reported so far.
caption:
Over 100 workers evacuated as a massive fire hits an 8-story sweater factory in Gazipur.

A fire broke out at the Metrics sweater factory in the Degerchala Fakir Market area of Gazipur city on Saturday afternoon.

The blaze started around 3:00 PM on the third floor of the eight-story building and quickly spread to surrounding areas.

Nine units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence, including units from Gazipur Chowrasta Modern, Konabari, Gazipur, and Rajendrapur stations, were deployed to control the blaze.

Firefighters reported that over 100 workers were safely evacuated from the building during the operation.

As of 4:45 PM, the fire had not yet been brought under control. The cause of the fire and the extent of the property damage have not been immediately known.

Gazipur Chowrasta Modern Fire Station officer Mo. Hiron Mia confirmed that efforts to control the fire are ongoing and no casualties have been reported so far.

caption:
1,608 people hospitalised in just 24 hours. Dengue deaths in Bangladesh continue to rise.

Bangladesh has reported six more deaths from dengue, with 1,608 new hospital admissions in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This brings the total death toll from the disease this year to 256. September has been the deadliest month so far, recording 148 deaths and 43,774 hospitalisations.

In the latest 24-hour count, Dhaka North and South City Corporations recorded 171 and 223 admissions respectively, while Chattogram saw 319 new admissions.

Other regions including Barishal (215), Khulna (276), and Rajshahi (132) also reported significant numbers of hospitalisations.

So far this year, 84,369 people have been hospitalised with dengue, while 78,482 have recovered and been discharged.

The DGHS has maintained records since 2000, noting that 2023 was the worst year on record with 321,179 hospitalisations and 1,705 deaths.
